name: Hapuku Lodge & Tree Houses
positioning: Lodge with tree houses on a working deer farm 10km north of Kaikoura on the east coast of the South Island, with views of the Kaikoura mountains and the Pacific; officially styled Hapuku Lodge + Tree Houses
best_for: Couples who want to sleep in a tree house high in a native kanuka grove
Families or groups wanting a two-bedroom tree house or the three-bedroom Olive House
Nature lovers who want stargazing, coastal walks and Kaikoura's marine wildlife

facts.text: The lodge is 10km north of the coastal marine town of Kaikoura, on the east coast of New Zealand's South Island.
The lodge is part of a working deer farm.
Tree House stays include deep-soaking baths with mountain or ocean views.
The Family Tree House has two ensuite bedrooms, an Upper and a Lower Branch, connected by an internal staircase.
The Olive House has sweeping views of the Kaikoura mountains and the Pacific Ocean.
Lodge Suites have a separate living area with a stone fireplace and panoramic views of the Kaikoura mountains and deer paddocks.
Lodge Suites have a deep two-person Japanese soaking tub.
From the sauna, the view drifts across the deer paddock to the Kaikoura mountains.
The signature Pinda Massage uses heated cotton pouches filled with sea salt, herbs and essential oils.
Quiet lanes past deer paddocks lead to the rugged coastline a kilometre from the Lodge.
All stays include a three-course dinner and gourmet breakfast each day.
Ingredients come from the lodge's organic kitchen garden, neighbouring farms and the Pacific.

highlights.text: The Tree Houses sit 10 metres (30 feet) above ground in the canopy of a native kanuka grove.
Guided stargazing is included for all guests, and the lodge is situated in the Dark Sky Sanctuary.
In the secluded secret garden, guests can book a private hot tub or play garden games as the sun sets over the seaward Kaikoura ranges.
The lodge has a heated outdoor mineral lap pool, spa pool, cold plunge and sauna, free for all guests.
The three-bedroom Olive House was once home to the estate's olive press.

considerations.text: The nearest international airport is Christchurch, about a 2 hour 35 minute drive away.
Rooms are not equipped for in-suite dining; all meals are served in the restaurant or courtyard.
Farm tours are not offered and guests may not enter the deer paddocks.
